next_mission_recommendation.mission_description: Extend the payment system to support recurring subscription plans alongside one-time credit purchases. Implement: (1) Monthly subscription tiers (Starter $29/mo = 5 credits, Pro $79/mo = 15 credits, Studio $199/mo = 50 credits) using Stripe Subscriptions API with automatic renewal, (2) Credit auto-replenishment that tops up credits at renewal and sends email notifications, (3) Subscription management UI where users can upgrade, downgrade, pause, or cancel their plan with Stripe Customer Portal integration, (4) Proration handling when switching plans mid-cycle, (5) Admin subscription analytics dashboard showing MRR (Monthly Recurring Revenue), churn rate, plan distribution, and at-risk accounts (failed payments), (6) Webhook handlers for all subscription lifecycle events (created, updated, deleted, payment_failed, trial_ending), (7) Grace period logic giving users 3 days after failed payment before credit suspension. All changes must be backward-compatible with existing one-time credit pack purchases, and the full test suite (193+ tests) must continue to pass.
next_mission_recommendation.rationale: The one-time credit purchase system is now production-ready. The natural next revenue evolution is recurring subscriptions, which dramatically improve revenue predictability (MRR vs one-time), reduce purchase friction for heavy users, and enable tier-based feature gating. Stripe Subscriptions is the logical extension of the Stripe integration already built — reusing existing infrastructure (webhook handler, credit provisioning, billing dashboard) while adding significant business value. Three cycles map cleanly to: Cycle 1 (subscription data model + basic subscribe/cancel flow), Cycle 2 (Customer Portal + proration + lifecycle webhooks), Cycle 3 (admin MRR analytics + grace periods + full test coverage).

final_report.summary: Across 3 cycles, a complete production-grade Stripe credit payment system was built and hardened for AI-StoryForge. Cycle 1 implemented the core payment flow: credit store UI with pricing tiers, Stripe checkout session creation, webhook handlers for payment confirmation, automatic credit provisioning, transaction logging in a new stripe_payments table, and a user billing dashboard with purchase history. Cycle 2 hardened the system: security hardening (CSRF, webhook signature verification, idempotency), admin financial oversight panel, rate limiting on payment endpoints, receipt page with full transaction details, email confirmation infrastructure, and 64 comprehensive payment tests all passing. Cycle 3 completed all production-readiness items: fixed cross-suite test isolation bug (DB_PATH pollution), added 7 mocked SMTP integration tests, implemented admin billing overview endpoint with HTML template and JSON API, documented Stripe key validation status, and confirmed all 193 tests pass end-to-end in any execution order.

challenges_overcome: Cross-suite test isolation: test_payment_mission.py polluted Config.DB_PATH at import time, causing test_cycle2.py admin tests to write to wrong database; fixed by hardcoding absolute path from __file__ instead of reading from Config
Webhook idempotency: concurrent webhook deliveries could double-credit users; solved with database UNIQUE constraint on payment_intent_id and per-intent row locking
No live Stripe keys available in environment: validated payment flow via synthetic webhook event injection in tests rather than real card charges
Admin auth separation: admin routes use separate session handling from user routes, required careful blueprint registration order to avoid 403s in tests
lessons_learned: Never read Config values at module import time in test files — Config may have been mutated by a previous test module's fixtures
Stripe webhook idempotency must be enforced at the database layer (UNIQUE constraint), not just application logic, to survive concurrent deliveries
SMTP email sending should always be optional/non-blocking — wrap in try/except and log failures, never let email failures block credit provisioning
When Stripe keys are unavailable, synthetic webhook injection provides excellent coverage of the full payment confirmation path
Admin billing endpoints should expose both HTML and JSON variants from the start — the JSON API makes testing trivial without browser automation
